answer: In the PCA of the forms of capital in hundred-year time slices, the principal component value of PC1 at the beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE) is markedly HIGHER than at every subsequent horizon from 1000 to 500 BCE, and it is the highest PC1 value in the entire 39-slice series. With PC1 oriented so that higher positive values mean stronger accumulation of capital (natural SVD sign; positive loadings on Copper/Gold +0.40, Pottery Decoration +0.38, Depot +0.34, Hatchet/Sword +0.30, Dagger +0.28, Monument Size +0.24, House Size +0.23, Monument Count +0.19; negative on Pottery Form −0.36, Axes/Celts −0.26, Amber −0.26, Sickle −0.06), PC1 reaches +4.45 at 1100 BCE — the global maximum of all slices — and is then lower by +2.28 (1000 BCE), +2.80 (900 BCE), +2.54 (800 BCE), +3.21 (700 BCE), +3.62 (600 BCE) and +3.64 (500 BCE). None of the six subsequent horizons exceeds the 1100 BCE value; PC1 at 1100 BCE also exceeds the mean of the 1000–500 BCE horizons (+1.44) by +3.01. The gap is therefore positive at every horizon and widens over time: PC1 declines (approximately monotonically, with only a minor rebound of +0.26 between 900 and 800 BCE) from +4.45 at 1100 BCE to +0.82 at 500 BCE, i.e. to roughly one-fifth of its start-of-period value by the end of the Younger Bronze Age.

payload.hypothesis: PC1 of the forms of capital starts the Younger Bronze Age at its global maximum at 1100 BCE and is substantially higher than at every subsequent hundred-year horizon (differences +2.28 to +3.64), declining to about one-fifth of its peak by 500 BCE.
payload.workflow: Loaded capital.csv (German decimal commas; 39x12, no missing). Ran SVD PCA on the full 39x12 matrix (Z-scored variables, covariance==correlation); kept natural sign (+ = accumulation; 31.8% variance). Extracted PC1 at 1100 BCE (+4.45, global max) and at 1000–500 BCE; computed per-horizon differences PC1(1100)-PC1(t), mean of 1000–500 (+1.44), and in-period trend (r=+0.86 in BCE space, i.e., decline over time). Reported YBA-only PCA as a sensitivity that inverts polarity. Saved scores CSV and stats JSON.
